Born at Saranac on 29 May 1918, son of Doctor Clarence Hutchins.
PFC, U.S. Army, World War II. About 1952 he and Leon "Duke" Elliott bought Harrison B. Parks's International Harvester
sales and service store on the East Main Street Road in Malone and opened as Elliott and Hutchins,
Inc. They sold IH tractors and farm machinery, Jamesway barn equipment, Homelite chain saws and IH refrigerators and
freezers, with Cliff Willis and Walt Ashlaw in the service shop.
In December 1953 he married Barbara Elenor Hammond at New Kensington, Pennsylvania.
The firm grew into Malone's largest privately owned industry, with its own fleet of trucks and tractor-trailers carrying
recreational products to dealers across the Northeast; by its 25th anniversary,
about 1977, company vehicles were logging more than 350,000 miles a year.
He was its vice president, living on Franklin Street.
A man who worked for the two partners for eleven years remembered them as opposites:
Duke in a three-piece suit, quiet and reserved; Dee in a sports jacket, loud and boisterous,
who would tell you himself, across the office, what needed doing, and who loved a party,
planning the dinners for the group at the snowmobile races.
It was, he said, the best job he ever had.
